children: Wall Street’s enthusiasm for artificial intelligence is helping technology stocks withstand a surge in interest rates that would normally put significant pressure on equity valuations, Bloomberg News reported Sunday.
The 10-year Treasury yield
recently topped 5.3% while the 30-year yield reached 5.69%, their highest levels since 2002. Yet the Nasdaq 100 closed at a record Friday and has gained 22% this year. The S&P 500 (
) is less than 1% below its August record, with Microsoft
, Nvidia
and Apple
among the biggest contributors to recent gains.

Investors are betting that strong earnings growth will justify elevated technology valuations. Third-quarter earnings per share for the tech sector are projected to rise more than 65%, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Overall S&P 500 earnings are expected to increase more than 24%, which would mark a third consecutive quarter of growth exceeding 20%.

The market increasingly depends on Big Tech earnings to offset the effects of high interest rates. That makes upcoming results from major AI companies particularly important. Strong profit growth could sustain the rally, but disappointing earnings or another sharp increase in Treasury yields could pressure valuations and expose the broader market's reliance on a relatively small group of technology stocks.
The AI investment boom also is changing the financial profiles of some of those companies. Alphabet
, Amazon
and Meta
have seen annual free cash flow turn negative as spending on data centers and other AI infrastructure accelerates. Meta
, Amazon
, Alphabet
, Microsoft
and Oracle
increasingly need outside financing to supplement internally generated cash, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.

Higher borrowing costs haven't damaged the credit ratings of the largest technology companies so far because expectations for earnings growth remain strong. However, greater reliance on debt makes rising rates more relevant to a group that previously was largely insulated by enormous cash balances and relatively low leverage.
Elsewhere in the market, higher rates are already taking a toll. The S&P 500 (
) trades at less than 19 times projected earnings, down from more than 21 times in May, while rate-sensitive and capital-intensive stocks outside the AI trade have come under greater pressure.

Investors also face inflation risks from elevated oil prices and the war involving Iran, along with the possibility of another Federal Reserve rate increase this year. A decline in oil prices could ease inflation and support stocks, but persistent inflation or a further jump in bond yields could test the AI rally. Some strategists see a 10-year Treasury yield approaching 6% as a level that could materially change the outlook for equities.

title: AI rally defies 24-yr high in Treasury yields, but risks are building
